_note: One short, hand-written, conservative blurb per anti-bot detector, keyed by the detector id without the detect- prefix. Only facts that are public and stable; when unsure, keep it generic. Signals are never written here: they come from detectors/antibot/*.json.
akamai: Akamai Bot Manager is the bot management product of Akamai Technologies, a CDN and security company. It is sold to large sites as part of Akamai's edge platform and aims to tell people, good bots and abusive automation apart.
aliyunwaf: Alibaba Cloud WAF is the web application firewall of Alibaba Cloud. Besides filtering attacks it can serve JavaScript challenges to clients it does not trust, which is why it shows up in front of many Chinese and some global sites.
amazon: Amazon's sign-in pages collect a client-side browser fingerprint that the login form submits with the credentials. It is part of Amazon's own anti-abuse tooling rather than a product other sites can buy.
anubis: Anubis is an open-source web gate from Techaro that asks each new visitor's browser to solve a small proof-of-work puzzle before the page loads. It was created to slow down AI crawlers and is deployed by many open-source and community sites.
aws-waf: AWS WAF is Amazon Web Services' web application firewall. Its Bot Control and challenge features can require a browser to run a JavaScript challenge and keep a token, so a plain HTTP client may be turned away.
azurefrontdoor: Azure Front Door is Microsoft's global content delivery and application delivery service for Azure. It can be combined with Azure's web application firewall, so seeing it tells you about the edge in front of a site, not always that bots are filtered.
botguard: BotGuard is Google's own client-side integrity and bot detection technology. It is used by Google services and by reCAPTCHA, and Google does not publish how it works.
castle: Castle is a security vendor that offers account-takeover, bot and abuse protection. Its browser script builds a request token that the site sends to Castle's API alongside login and sensitive actions.
cheq: CHEQ is a go-to-market security company that sells bot, invalid-traffic and fraud prevention, mostly for advertising and marketing traffic.
cloudflare-waitingroom: Cloudflare Waiting Room is a Cloudflare feature that puts visitors in a queue when a site expects more traffic than its origin can handle. It is a traffic-control tool, not a bot detector, but the queue page still stops simple scrapers.
cloudflare: Cloudflare Bot Management is Cloudflare's paid bot detection product, delivered from its global network. Cloudflare also runs free challenge pages, so a Cloudflare challenge does not by itself mean the paid product is enabled.
datadome: DataDome is a French bot and online fraud protection vendor. It scores requests with a JavaScript tag and server-side signals and can answer with a challenge or a block page.
ddosguard: DDoS-Guard is a hosting and DDoS-protection provider that works as a reverse proxy. It can show a browser check to visitors it wants to verify.
deepseek-pow: DeepSeek's chat web app asks the browser to solve a proof-of-work challenge before it accepts a chat request. It is the service's own protection rather than a product sold to other sites.
f5: F5 BIG-IP Application Security Manager (ASM) is F5's web application firewall. It is usually run by a site's own infrastructure team and can include bot defence features.
fastly: Fastly Bot Management is the bot detection product of Fastly, an edge cloud provider. It is delivered through Fastly's edge network and, per its detector, may also run client-side checks.
fingerprintjs: FingerprintJS is a browser fingerprinting library, available as an open-source version and a commercial Pro service from Fingerprint. Its BotD library is a separate open-source bot detection tool. Finding it shows a site collects device signals, not necessarily that it blocks bots.
forter: Forter is a fraud prevention vendor for online commerce. Its script fingerprints the browser and the site sends the resulting token with checkout and login decisions.
hunt: Hunt is an anti-bot system seen on some betting platforms. It collects a browser fingerprint and may follow up with an interactive captcha when it decides to block.
incapsula: Incapsula is the former name of the Imperva cloud web application firewall and CDN. It combines WAF rules with bot protection and is often recognised by its cookies.
iovation: iovation is a device recognition and fraud prevention service now part of TransUnion as TruValidate. Its script collects a device blackbox that the site submits with sensitive actions.
jiasule: Jiasule, also written Chuangyu Shield, is an anti-DDoS and web protection service from Knownsec in China. It often presents a JavaScript gate before a page loads.
kasada: Kasada is a bot mitigation vendor. It runs client-side checks in the browser and attaches proof to later requests, so requests made without that proof are likely to be refused.
kount: Kount, part of Equifax, is a payment fraud prevention company. Its Device Data Collector gathers browser information that the merchant's backend sends to Kount for a risk decision.
meetrics: Meetrics is a media measurement company that has offered ad viewability and ad-fraud measurement tags. The detector flags older integrations that still reference its script, which may no longer work.
netacea: Netacea is a bot management vendor that works without a page script on every request, reading traffic at the edge or the server instead. Its cookies are the usual visible trace, and their names can be changed per customer.
ocule: Ocule was a bot protection service that was later absorbed by hCaptcha. Pages that still reference it are generally old integrations.
openai-sentinel: Sentinel is the name of the anti-abuse layer used by ChatGPT and OpenAI sign-in. It issues challenges to the browser before some requests. It protects OpenAI's own services and is not a product for other sites.
perimeterx: PerimeterX is now part of HUMAN Security. Its bot defender places a script on the page and scores visitors by behaviour and device signals, and can answer with a press-and-hold style challenge.
queueit: Queue-it is a virtual waiting room service. It sends visitors to a queue page when a site is overloaded, for example during a ticket or product sale. It controls traffic rather than detecting bots, though it also offers bot filtering options.
radware: Radware Bot Manager, formerly ShieldSquare, is the bot management product of Radware. Radware also sells a cloud WAF, and the detector looks for traces of both.
reblaze: Reblaze is a cloud web security platform that includes a web application firewall, DDoS protection and bot management.
riskified: Riskified is an e-commerce fraud prevention company. A script on storefronts sends browser and session data that supports its payment and account abuse decisions.
ruishu: Ruishu is a Chinese bot protection product from River Security. It typically delivers heavily obfuscated JavaScript that sets dynamic cookies before the real page is served.
seon: SEON is a fraud prevention company. Its JavaScript agent gathers device and network signals that feed its risk scoring.
shapesecurity: Shape Security, acquired by F5, built enterprise bot defence aimed at fraud, credential stuffing and automation on login and checkout flows.
sift: Sift is a digital trust and fraud prevention platform. Its page snippet reports device and page-view data to Sift for risk scoring.
siteground-captcha: SG-CAPTCHA is the anti-bot challenge used by SiteGround hosting. Visitors that look automated are sent to a challenge page that must be passed before the site loads.
sucuri: Sucuri is a website security company whose cloud WAF and CDN sit in front of a site to filter attacks and unwanted traffic.
threatmetrix: ThreatMetrix is a device identification and fraud prevention service now owned by LexisNexis Risk Solutions. It profiles the visitor's device and sends the result to a decision engine.
vercel: Vercel Firewall is the security layer of the Vercel hosting platform. It includes configurable rules, an Attack Mode challenge page and a BotID check.
wordfence: Wordfence is a popular WordPress security plugin. It adds a firewall, rate limiting and login protection to a single WordPress site.
yundun: Yundun is a Chinese cloud security provider offering a cloud WAF and anti-DDoS service. Its checks are commonly seen on Chinese websites.
